findings.title: Recognition through traces across changed status
findings.claim: Yusuf's one-sided recognition can be understood as recognition through identity-bearing traces that survive a changed status, giving him access to shared history that the brothers no longer possess.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier at 12:58:6:2 is Yusuf's completed recognition. The wider triggers at 12:19, 12:54, and 12:93 supply concealed status, public authority, and a deliberate garment trace; their contact turns the focus from a bare visual mismatch into unequal access to surviving identity marks.
findings.reader_payoff: The asymmetry becomes a difference in access to a person's surviving signs and history, not merely a failure of simultaneous visual recognition.
findings.containment: The packet does not establish which exact trace Yusuf used, and this does not convert the brothers' failure into deliberate denial. The ordinary one-sided recognition and nonrecognition remain intact; the trace mechanism is a qualified global inference.

epistemic.reason: The reader walk is legacy-unbound and explicitly inferential. The supplied connection rows provide wider Arabic and narrative triggers but lack target morphology, so the trace-status mechanism remains qualified.

findings.title: Asymmetric recognition as controlled information
findings.claim: The asymmetry in knowing gives Yusuf a temporary informational advantage: he can receive, test, and redirect the returning family while the brothers remain unaware of who stands before them.
findings.mechanism: The recognition carrier at 12:58:6:2 meets the nonrecognition carrier at 12:58:9:1. The earlier rupture and concealment at 12:9 and 12:19, Yusuf's entrusted office at 12:54, and the later confrontation and disclosure at 12:89-90 make the mirrored knowledge states operational rather than merely descriptive.
findings.reader_payoff: The meeting becomes an encounter with controlled disclosure, where one side can shape the next movement while the other side still reads the situation without its decisive identity.
findings.containment: This does not replace the literal arrival, recognition, and nonrecognition, and it does not claim permanent superiority. The later disclosure remains a live reversal of the temporary advantage.

epistemic.reason: The citable cross-run publication supplies exact focus anchors and the three named branch records. The operational consequence is retained, while its wider narrative reach and the qualified B004 identity remain explicitly bounded.

findings.title: A temporary asymmetry that later reverses
findings.claim: The one-sided recognition in 12:58 is temporary in the story's wider movement: later confrontation and self-disclosure return recognition to both sides.
findings.mechanism: The focus states that Yusuf recognizes the brothers while they do not recognize him. The supplied 12:89 connection brings their past act to speech, and 12:90 supplies self-disclosure; the contact turns the present nonrecognition into a delayed stage in a reversible recognition arc.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the current imbalance as a live interval in which recognition is held on one side and then returned, rather than as the story's final state.
findings.containment: The later resolution does not erase the present nonrecognition or prove that concealment has only one motive. It bounds the asymmetry as temporary within this supplied story movement.

epistemic.reason: The retrospective walk is legacy-unbound, while the 12:89-90 connection rows provide exact target Arabic as discovery nominations. The reversal is retained with explicit qualification rather than treated as a ranked conclusion.

findings.title: Brotherhood as a relation under testing

findings.mechanism: The focus carrier إِخْوَةُ at 12:58:2:1 names literal brothers. The supplied wider triggers at 12:9 and 12:11 preserve the earlier plot and assurances, while 12:80 and 12:92 return the relation through covenant, remembered failure, and non-retaliation; their contact makes the family label a pressured relation rather than a neutral group descriptor.
findings.reader_payoff: The word brothers arrives with a history that the present meeting silently carries: kinship is present, but its trust must pass through testing before it can function as restored relation.
findings.containment: This activates the core kinship facet only. It does not turn the word into general friendship, activate the separate binding-ring branch, or claim that the noun alone assigns moral blame.

epistemic.reason: The finding is an independent synthesis from the exact focus branch and connection nominations. The connection records are discovery evidence with missing target morphology, so the wider relational effect remains qualified.

findings.title: Entry before open reception
findings.claim: The brothers' entry upon Yusuf is the first threshold of a wider movement that later turns entry into open family reception.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier دَخَلُوا at 12:58:4:2 places the group inside Yusuf's presence and authority. The exact 12:99 connection repeats the entry upon Yusuf and then shows shelter and welcome, so the same act returns with its relation openly restored; that contact makes the present entry a threshold rather than a completed reunion.
findings.reader_payoff: The scene's movement into Yusuf's presence acquires a delayed shape: the brothers can enter before they can belong openly, and a later entry supplies the changed relational outcome.
findings.containment: The focus verse does not itself announce the later welcome, and not every occurrence of entering shares this arc. The finding is limited to the supplied parallel and preserves the present scene's unresolved recognition.

epistemic.reason: The focus branch and carrier are exact, while 12:99 is a connection nomination with supplied Arabic but no target morphology. The delayed reception is therefore a qualified global resonance.
